content.comment_body: Hi, I'm experimenting with [product_name] Web Editor to create websites that interact with my [product_name]. Everything works well so far. Now I've set up an unrelated website running on a server in the same network as my [product_name]. I want to know if it's possible to control my [product_name] from this other site. While I could embed the [product_name] Web Editor website from the SD card into my page via a [url], I can't customize how it looks or make it adapt responsively to different devices. Is there a way to control buttons or read statuses from the [product_name] Web Editor – for instance, using HTML GET or POST requests? The [document] mentions this approach, but it's vague and lacks practical examples. Could anyone provide direction or point to examples? Many thanks!

To access a website stored on an SD card from another site, follow these recommendations: • Host the content using a local server like Apache or Nginx. • Access SD card files via the server's URL (e.g., http://localhost/website/ or a relevant path). • Ensure the web server can read from the SD card. • Link your second website to the hosted SD card content using correct URLs. If you need more detailed setup instructions for your system, let me know!
Host your SD card site locally using a web server (such as Apache or Nginx) to make it available via LAN or a public IP. Configure CORS policies to permit access between your websites.

If you access the device settings via its IP, a secure option would be using a reverse proxy on your local web server in the same network. If your server faces the Internet, it's recommended to have two network cards (one public, one private in the [product_name] network). Apply redirection or use a reverse proxy to avoid exposing the [product_name]'s IP and make access as secure as possible with HTTPS and authentication.
English is the preferred language in this forum. Please submit posts in English. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: Users aim to integrate control and status feedback of [product_name] devices into customizable, responsive external web interfaces. The documentation for [product_name] Web Editor is seen as unclear, especially regarding technical details for interaction through standard web requests like HTML GET/POST from other web apps. Concerns revolve around adapting interfaces, enabling secure access, and ensuring technical feasibility for remote/cross-origin control.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear instructions and working examples for controlling [product_name] features (such as button actions and status queries) with web requests from external sites. Sufficient documentation is needed to develop adaptive custom interfaces without losing device control or feedback.
